title: Luel Speech is now available for public access | Luel
summary: Specialist production audio for unrepresented languages: eight voices across Tibetan, Darija, Masri and Dzongkha, in the Studio or over the API.
body_markdown:
Commercial speech technology covers[about one percent of the world's languages](https://www.luel.ai/blog/the-tts-gap-and-why-were-building) , and where an Arabic dialect voice exists at all it is usually trained on the formal written standard, not the dialect people actually speak. Ü-Tsang Tibetan and Dzongkha do not get even that: no major platform lists either one.


That is the gap Luel Speech fills, and as of today it is public.


## Luel Speech Studio


Paste a line, pick a language and a voice, hear it back, nothing to install and no key to mint. Pick a language below to see the line its voices read.
